scope: Only the two original full texts specified in CODEX_V02_VocabPriorBench.txt; directed sections, no open-ended review.

sources.title: N-Gram Memories at Two Bits: Quantizing Lookup Tables in Large Language Models
sources.version_evidence: Official abstract page states last revised 21 Oct 2026 (this version, v3) and gives the v3 submission timestamp; explicit v3 HTML was also successfully opened.
locators: Section 2.1 Conditional Memory as Selective Lookup, equation 1
Section 4.3 Effect of Row-wise Scaling, Table 4
Appendix E.2 Scale choices and data / Predictions and evaluation / Observed gains and prediction errors, Table 19
Appendix F.3 Perturbations through the readout

verified_evidence.scale_controls: Global gain, per-row LS and original-row norm restoration; LS and restored norm share codes and bytes.
verified_evidence.held_out_prediction: Gain rules fixed before test splits. Primary local-quadratic predictor fails at multiple operating points; secondary calibration quadratic has correct direction in the five resolved cells. Some code/Wikipedia test texts reuse the earlier benchmark.
verified_evidence.mathematical_boundary: For e=ru, unit decoded v and c=u^T v, row-coordinate LS gain is rc; norm-restoring gain is r. Network-metric optimal gain need not equal either.
verified_evidence.perturbation_boundary: F.3 compares equal-energy norm, direction and projection-subspace perturbations in selective memory; not random-student output training.

sources.project_difference: Selective conditional-memory lookup in an existing model versus a frozen dense output table with a retrained random student; setting difference alone is not substantive novelty.

sources.title: OneBit: Towards Extremely Low-bit Large Language Models
sources.venue: 38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024)
sources.metadata_evidence: Title and eight authors are on PDF page 1; the footer identifies NeurIPS 2024.

verified_evidence.representation: Sign matrix with two FP16 value vectors g and h; W approximately sign(W) elementwise-multiplied by an outer-product amplitude ab^T.
verified_evidence.training: Quantization-aware knowledge distillation trains the underlying quantized-layer parameters and g/h, using teacher logits and hidden states.
verified_evidence.storage_boundary: The paper discusses INT1-packed sign matrices at inference; this project uses FP32 frozen code tables and does not inherit that storage/compute result.

sources.project_difference: Frozen low-dimensional output-table controls with an independently initialized student, rather than pretrained-weight quantization and teacher distillation; not a novelty proof.
not_verified: All sign/amplitude methods outside this directed source

claims_not_supported_as_novel: A held-out gain prediction test by itself
A different model setting or a residual by itself

errata_evidence.candidate_metric: Unweighted maximum cosine-neighbor margin; training frequencies stratify/sort queries, not weight the margin.
errata_evidence.v02_requirement: Record each trajectory UTC and monotonic start adjacent at the same code location; actual execution verification belongs to the V0.2 snapshot/log audit.
